thread:
maya: heads up — noticed a weird capacity hole in eu-west yesterday, looks like a bunch of GPUs got tombstoned and never came back into the pool. apps hit increased latency at ~20:15 UTC.

alec: which pool? dedicated or shared?

maya: shared-edge-eu2 mostly. some nodes moved to `TOMBSTONED` state in our allocator due to short-lived NIC flaps, then the hysteresis prevented rejoining for ~40m. capacity reported healthy but scheduler couldn't bind.

priya: oof. so allocator thinks it's fine but scheduler has fewer usable slots? any logs?

maya: pasted the controller probe output below:
```
$ rctlctl get node node-eu2-45 --json
{
  "state": "tombstoned",
  "last_transition": 1729002900,
  "nic_errors": 3,
  "egress_saturation": false
}
```

andre: can we reduce the tombstone hysteresis window? current is 30m IIRC. that'll reduce outage but increases churn risk.

maya: agreed, but also root cause is NIC IRQ storm on that rack. it's causing intermittent kernel drops which our health-check marks as transient. tombstone was protective.

alec: short-term: can we add a routing policy that avoids placing low-qos tenants on racks with >1 transient error in last 10m? quick patch in fleet router.

priya: yes, we can add an egress-signal soft-avoid. patch idea: when `err_count >= 2` in 600s, tag rack `soft-quarantine`. router reduces weight by 0.8.

andre: +1. also propose a background sweep to force re-eval of tombstoned nodes every 5m instead of 30m if there is free capacity pressure.

maya: testing a small change now — toggling tombstone re-eval from 30m -> 5m for edge pools only. will monitor for flapping.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by maya on branch `fix/tombstone-reval`. CI: passed. canary: 2/6 nodes in eu2-edge.

alec: nice. what's the rollback plan if flapping increases?

maya: auto-rollout will revert after 3 flaps in 15m. logs will tag `tombstone-flap` and we have a dashboard alert.

priya: long-term: we should correlate NIC IRQs with tenant noisy patterns. noisy-tenant detection + proactive shielding sounds right. maybe move noisy tenants to dedicated slices temporarily.

andre: cost question — moving noisy tenants to dedicated increases cost. need to measure delta: shielding vs dedicated pool. add to next week's Ops meeting.

maya: captured. I'll create a short perf/cost eval. quick note: in this case QoS-tier 3 tenants were the majority of traffic during the incident.

alec: also add a small router rule to prefer quantized/quantized-compat models to fall back to lighter variants if pool capacity drops 15% in a region. reduces tail latency spikes.

priya: ack. I'll draft the router PR and the cost eval doc.

maya: thanks — will watch the canary for 60m and post updates. :eyes:

infra-bot: canary metrics (10m): p99 latency +8% on shared-edge-eu2, tombstone re-eval events: 4, flaps: 0.

maya: initial canary looks ok. leaving re-eval at 5m for edge-only for next 24h. filing follow-ups: runbook update + cost comparison + router PR.

alec: perfect. ping me if p99 > +12% or flaps > 1.

maya: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
